name: Harp
description: A concert harp with koto and guzheng strings: every note is its own plucked string that rings on after the key is let go, over a soundboard, with the other strings ringing in sympathy.

params.name: Strings
params.description: The kind of string. Harp is soft gut under a finger; Koto is a dry string under a hard pick; Guzheng is brighter steel that rings longer. Applies from the next note.

params.name: Pluck
params.description: Where along the string it is plucked. Low is near the end: thin, nasal and bright. High is the middle: round and hollow. Applies from the next note.

params.name: Touch
params.description: How hard the finger or pick is. Low is a soft pad with a dark, rounded start; high is a hard edge with a bright attack and a click. Applies from the next note.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long the strings ring. Low strings always ring much longer than high ones. Applies from the next note.

params.name: Damp
params.description: How much letting go of a key stops its string. At zero nothing stops it and notes ring into each other; at full a hand mutes it at once.

params.name: Halo
params.description: How much the strings that are already ringing pick up each new note and ring along with it. It needs other notes still sounding to be heard.

params.name: Sweep
params.description: Rolls notes that are played together into a glissando from the lowest to the highest, spread over this time. At zero a chord is plucked together.

params.name: Bend
params.description: Presses each note sharp a moment after it is plucked, the way a koto player leans on the string behind the bridge. It only ever rises. Applies from the next note.

params.name: Body
params.description: How much of the wooden soundboard is heard. Low is the bare strings; high is fuller and woodier, more hollow on Koto and Guzheng.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many strings ring at once.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit, from the plucked-string, concert harp and koto/guzheng sections of the project's string research. What is modelled: one undamped string per pitch on the kit's extended Karplus-Strong loop (Jaffe and Smith 1983; the loop filter of Välimäki et al. 1996) with a pluck-position comb and decay times set per register; the pedal harp's soft finger-pad pluck near the middle of flexible gut and nylon strings; the hard plectrum of the koto and guzheng near the bridge, their upward-only pressed bends and the pitch of a hard pluck settling as the tension relaxes; the guzheng's stiffer wound-steel strings; re-plucking a ringing string as a finger landing on it; sympathetic ringing as feedback between the strings that sound; a shared soundboard of six broad resonances. What is simplified: one polarisation per string (no beating), a soundboard of fixed band-pass resonators instead of a measured body, sympathetic ringing only among strings that have been played (its strength is held under a stability bound, so each string receives less as more ring), no pedals, no diatonic or pentatonic tuning table, no vibrato. Choices, not measurements of any instrument: the decay curves by register (about 7 s at C2, 2.7 s at middle C and 1 s at C6 for the harp; about 2.2 s and 4.5 s at middle C for koto and guzheng), the soundboard frequencies, the bend timing (starts 80 ms after the pluck, about a fifth of a second long), the settling depth (up to 12 cents for koto, 8 for guzheng) and the guzheng's inharmonicity (B = 1.2e-4). The research these come from rests on general acoustics knowledge; nobody has compared the result with a recording by ear. It uses no samples and is not an emulation of any one instrument.
